body.p: Please reconsider the present application in view of the above amendments and the following remarks. Applicant thanks the Examiner for carefully considering the present application.
I. Disposition of Claims

Claim 1 has been amended by incorporating "wherein a material of the marker comprises a material with light-absorbing properties, and the first absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the first optical pulse and the second absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the second optical pulse are capable of being acquired based on an absorption spectrum in an imaging wavelength range of the marker" in the claim.
Claim 2 has been amended in the manner similar to claim 1.
Claim 11 has been amended by incorporating claim 12.
New claim 21 has been added.
Support for the amendment can be found throughout the specification and at least in paragraphs [0067] and [0080]-[0082] of the specification as originally filed.
No new matters are added.
II. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §112(b)
In the Office Action, claims 1-2, 6-10 and 14-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) as allegedly being indefinite, page 2.

In response, applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 has been amended by incorporating "wherein a material of the marker comprises a material with light-absorbing properties, and the first absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the first optical pulse and the second absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the second optical pulse are capable of being acquired based on an absorption spectrum in an imaging wavelength range of the marker" in the claim. Amended claim 1 clearly recites that the marker is physical substance, rather than a shape or parameter given from the light source to illuminate a region of interest, so that the amended claims more clearly comply with 35 U.S.C. § 112(b).
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b).
III. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1)
Claims 1-7 and 9-19 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by Li et al. (US2013/0109941A1), page 3.
Applicant respectfully traverses. However, to advance the prosecution and without conceding to the rejections, claim 1 has been amended to moot the rejections.
The amended claim 1 recites, among other elements, that:
receiving a first acoustic wave generated by the target tissue absorbing the first
optical pulse to acquire a first photoacoustic signal, and receiving a third acoustic wave generated by a marker absorbing the first optical pulse to acquire a third photoacoustic
signal
receiving a second acoustic wave generated by the target tissue absorbing the
second optical pulse to acquire a second photoacoustic signal, and receiving a fourth acoustic wave generated by the marker absorbing the second optical pulse to acquire a
fourth photoacoustic signal
correcting a signal intensity of the first photoacoustic signal based on a signal

intensity of the third photoacoustic signal together with a first absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the first optical pulse, and correcting a signal intensity of the second photoacoustic signal based on the fourth photoacoustic signal together with a
second absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the second optical pulse
wherein a material of the marker comprises a material with light-absorbing

properties, and the first absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the first optical pulse and the second absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the second optical pulse are capable of being acquired based on an absorption spectrum in an
imaging wavelength range of the marker. (Feature A)
Applicant respectfully submits that Li fails to disclose Feature A of the amended claim 1 for the following reasons.

As the marker is defined as "a material with light-absorbing properties", it is made clear that the present invention is directed to correcting the photoacoustic signal generated by the laser irradiating the target tissue with the photoacoustic signal generated by the laser irradiating the marker with light-absorbing properties, so as to obtain the corrected photoacoustic signal.

In the Office Action, the Examiner asserted that paragraph [0077] of Li discloses the marker. Paragraph [0077] of Li discloses "step 610 need not include performing a measurement, and may include accessing empirical information (e.g., historical measurement, historical data, sample population data), a mathematical model, and other suitable information, or any combination thereof...step 610 may include processor 312 using a mathematical model to characterize one or more optical parameters based on suitable recalled optical information. In some embodiments, step 610 may include receiving optical information from operator input. For example, an operator may input one or more values or descriptors to system 300, and processor 312 may then characterize optical properties of the subject. In an illustrative example, an operator may input the subject's age and skin color into system 300, and processor 312 may determine effective optical properties based on these descriptors". That is, Li discloses that the operation inputs the skin color of the subject into the system without performing the measurement.
However, as stated above, the marker recited in the amended claim 1 includes the material with light-absorbing properties, which is completely different from the skin color input by the operator.

Therefore, it is submitted that Li fails to disclose the marker that includes a material with light-absorbing properties, and the first absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the first optical pulse and the second absorption coefficient of the marker with respect to the second optical pulse are capable of being acquired based on an absorption spectrum in an imaging wavelength range of the marker, let alone receiving the acoustic wave generated by the marker absorbing the optical pulse.

Furthermore, Li (see paragraph [0042]) discloses "encoder 42 may contain information about sensor unit 12, such as what type of sensor it is (e.g., where the sensor is intended to be placed on a subject), the wavelength(s) of light emitted by light source 16, the intensity of light emitted by light source 16 (e.g., output wattage or Joules), the mode of light source 16 (e.g., pulsed versus CW), any other suitable information, or any combination thereof. This information may be used by monitor 14 to select appropriate algorithms, lookup tables and/or calibration coefficients stored in monitor 14 for calculating the subject's physiological parameters". That is,
Li discloses using the photoacoustic information and optical information to calculate the subject's physiological parameters.

However, Li is silent about correcting the signal intensity of the photoacoustic signal related to acoustic wave generated by the tissue absorbing the optical pulse based on the signal intensity of the photoacoustic signal related to acoustic wave generated by the marker absorbing the optical pulse together with the absorption coefficient.

In view of the above, Li is silent about the marker with the material with the light- absorbing properties, let alone using the marker with the light-absorbing properties (of which the absorption coefficient are capable of being acquired) to correct the signal intensity of the photoacoustic signal related to acoustic wave generated by the tissue absorbing the optical pulse based on the signal intensity of the photoacoustic signal related to acoustic wave generated by the marker absorbing the optical pulse together with the absorption coefficient.
Therefore, it is submitted that Li fails to disclose Feature A of the amended claim 1.

Therefore, amended independent claim 1 is patentable over Li. For at least the similar reasons, the amended independent claim 2 is also patentable over Li. The dependent claims ultimately depend from the allowable independent claims and thus are patentable at least due to their dependency. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §102.
IV. Allowable Subject Matter
Applicant thanks the Examiner for the indication of allowable subject matter of claims 8 and 20, page 8.
As discussed above, independent claims 1-2 are allowable. Claims 8 and 20 ultimately depend from allowable independent claim 2, and thus are allowable at least due to their dependency.
In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
